title: Region-aware progressive steering with capacity cushions and latency SLOs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: We frequently observe tail-latency spikes in secondary regions during cross-region failover events. Current steering is largely latency-first with hard geo-pinning toggles; this can overcommit small regional pools and trigger downstream circuit breakers, causing longer overall outages for degraded customers. Goal: Implement a progressive steering policy that combines: 1) a continuous latency score, 2) an explicit regional capacity cushion (soft budget), and 3) soft geo-locking for sticky sessions. The policy must interact with circuit breakers and admission control so that we shed low-priority requests before cascading into SLO violations for higher-priority customers.
proposal_summary: Introduce a Region-Aware Progressive Steering (RAPS) controller that calculates a composite score per candidate region: composite_score = w_latency * normalized_p95 + w_capacity * (1 - capacity_utilization_fraction) + w_fidelity * geo_affinity_penalty. Steering picks the lowest composite_score subject to: (a) not exceeding the region's cushion budget, (b) respecting hard-exclusion lists (maintenance/blackouts), (c) honoring per-customer pin preferences for a configurable fraction of requests. When a region's circuit breaker trips, RAPS reroutes using a graduated ramp to remaining regions and temporarily increases cushion budgets for nearby regions to absorb KV cache warmup costs. Admission control integrates with token accounting to preferentially shed requests by priority labels and by estimated token cost.
design_considerations: Weight tuning: default w_latency=0.6, w_capacity=0.3, w_fidelity=0.1 but must be adjustable per fleet and per-route
Cushion calculation: cushion = min(allocated_capacity * cushion_fraction, absolute_min_margin). Start cushion_fraction at 12% for small regions, 6% for large regions
Soft geo-locking: a request can be soft-pinned for N minutes; after N, steering can move it if significant capacity/latency delta exists
Circuit breaker integration: when CB state=OPEN, RAPS reduces selected region's weight to infinity (exclude) and ramps traffic using exponential backoff windows to avoid thundering herd
Cache warmup penalty: when routing to cold region, apply temporary capacity penalty to account for KV cache miss rate and higher token cost
Interplay with batching: prefer regions with lower average batch size variance to keep token-level latency stable
acceptance_criteria: Can simulate a single-region outage and show no more than 10% increase in p95 for high-priority customers after ramp stabilization
Under test load, secondary regions should not exceed cushion utilization by more than 5% during a 10-minute failover window
Telemetry includes per-region cushion utilization, composite_score distribution, and per-route shed counts
E2E test: fail CB in primary region and verify staged ramp to secondaries with KV warmup penalty applied (log evidence in traces)
Feature flag gating present: raps.beta (off by default for existing customers)
Docs: Console UI update and runbook for on-call describing how to tune weights and cushions
rollout_plan: 1) Implement RAPS controller behind raps.beta flag; unit tests and simulation harness in steerbox-service. 2) Canary 5% on internal staging namespaces for 48h, collect cushion/utilization metrics. 3) Gradual ramp: 5 -> 25 -> 50% for low-latency routes over two weeks. 4) Enable soft geo-locking for a small set of customers and monitor affinity churn. 5) Promote to default for selected fleets once no regressions observed.
metrics_and_alerts: route.p95.high_priority increase > 10% baseline -> Trigger SLO regression alert
composite_score.skew -> Dashboard widget showing median vs 95th
telemetry_and_logs: Emit structured events: raps.decision(region, request_id, reason, composite_score, cushion_state). Add trace spans for 'raps.evaluate' with tags for latency_component, capacity_component, fidelity_penalty. Export cushion snapshots to metrics every 10s. Link to telemetry dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/raps-cushion
testing_and_simulation: Add simulation scenarios to steerbox-sim: cold-start failover, multi-region partial degradation, prioritized-client flood. Use synthetic KV hit/miss models to validate warmup penalty. Create load tests that mix embeddings and streaming generation workloads to ensure token-cost-aware shedding behaves as expected.
migration_and_backward_compatibility: RAPS must fall back to existing latency-first router when feature flag off. Provide a compatibility shim so that pinned sessions retain previous node affinity until TTL expires. Ensure API and SDK behavior unchanged; routing decisions are internal only.
security_and_privacy: No customer data is logged in events. Use only anonymized request hashes in telemetry. Review required if we expose per-customer cushion usage in public dashboards (currently internal-only).
notes_and_tradeoffs: - Tradeoff: prioritizing capacity may increase median latency for some requests but reduces large-scale cascading failures. - Tradeoff: cushion sizing across heterogeneous regions is heuristic-driven; we will add ML-driven cushion tuning later. - Decision: favour conservative ramping to avoid KV cache storms even though it delays failover completion by a few seconds.
